question: The Sokli mining project in Finland has applied for recognition as a strategic project under the Critical Raw Materials Act1. This project previously faced the rejection of environmental and water permits by Finland’s Supreme Administrative Court in 2022 due to significant environmental risks.

Recent developments indicate that the project promoter intends to proceed with test mining activities without a full environmental impact assessment, and has signalled the possibility of applying for derogations if permits are not granted. 1.

Can the Commission confirm that, prior to any designation of strategic project status, it will verify full compliance with the requirements of the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive2, in particular with regard to assessing projects as a whole and preventing circumvention of the Directive through the artificial splitting of projects3?
How does the Commission assess the compatibility of the project with the Water Framework Directive4, given the potential impacts on sensitive river systems?
Can the Commission confirm whether projects that previously failed to obtain environmental permits due to significant risks can qualify as ‘strategic projects’ under the Critical Raw Materials Act?

Regulation (EU) 2024/1252 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 establishing a framework for ensuring a secure and sustainable supply of critical raw materials and amending Regulations (EU) No 168/2013, (EU) 2018/858, (EU) 2018/1724 and (EU) 2019/1020 (OJ L, 2024/1252, 3.5.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1252/oj).

Directive 2011/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment (OJ L 26, 28.1.2012, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2011/92/oj). Article 2(1) and Annex III point 1(c) on cumulation https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A02011L0092-20140515.

Directive 2000/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2000 establishing a framework for Community action in the field of water policy, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A02000L0060-20141120.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.7.2026) The second selection round of Strategic Projects under the Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA)1 is ongoing. The assessment is conducted with the help of external experts and in consultation with the Critical Raw Materials Board. The Commission cannot comment on whether projects have applied and cannot prejudge possible outcomes of the assessment.

With regard to the sustainability selection criterion, the Commission conducts an overall assessment of a project’s compliance with relevant EU or national law, including the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive2 and the Water Framework Directive (WFD)3.

Without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, Member States are primarily responsible for ensuring compliance with EU law and for appointing the competent authorities for the required permitting procedures.

The competent authorities are in charge of the environmental impact assessment process for raw material projects where required, and of determining the scope of such environmental impact assessments4. In the case of a risk of deterioration of water bodies under the WFD, the authorisation can only be granted subject to strict conditions5.

The Strategic Project assessment focuses on the project’s fulfilment of the selection criteria defined in Article 6 of the CRMA on the basis of the project development status at the time of submission. In accordance with Article 7(8) of the CRMA, the Member State whose territory is concerned can raise its objection to a proposed project, following which a project shall not be recognised as a Strategic Project.
Through this process, permitting developments at national level as well as possible project evolvement can be taken into account as part of the Strategic Project assessment.
